title: Season 2, Ep 6: RAG as a Service
oneliner: When every team builds its own document pipelines, vector indexes, and hybrid search, the platform becomes a mess - offer RAG once, as a shared service.
says: Development teams across the organization build AI projects with different architectures - RAG, ReAct, human-in-the-loop. Each team building RAG must create document pipelines, vector indexing, and hybrid search (dense and sparse). When many teams each build these, the platform becomes a mess - so RAG should be offered as a centralized service.
explained: RAG - retrieval-augmented generation - is the pattern behind nearly every enterprise assistant: before the model answers, the system retrieves the relevant documents and hands them over as context. Its components are real engineering: pipelines that ingest and chunk documents, vector indexes that make them searchable by meaning, and hybrid search that combines semantic (dense) and keyword (sparse) matching so both 'similar meaning' and 'exact term' queries work.

The platform failure he describes is duplication with divergence: ten teams, ten chunking strategies, ten index configurations, ten subtly different answer qualities - and nobody can say which is right. RAG-as-a-Service turns the hard parts into a product: teams submit documents, the platform owns pipelines, indexes, and retrieval quality, and evaluation (next episode) measures the output. Retrieval quality stops being a lottery per team.
takeaway: Centralize the retrieval stack - document pipelines, vector indexes, hybrid search - so every team's assistant answers from the same quality bar.
